name: Hydraulic front shovel
subtitle: 140 t class, 7.5 m3 bucket -- CAT 6015 / PC1250 / EX1200 family
summary: The loading half of a shovel-dumper system. A face shovel digs into a blasted vertical face, swings about 90 degrees and bottom-dumps into a truck. Four to five passes should fill one dumper -- if it takes more, the pair is mismatched and both machines lose money.
specs: approx. 12 m -- governs safe face height
safety: Never approach the machine until the operator has grounded the bucket and signalled you in -- the swing radius is a no-go zone.
Trucks reverse in on the operator's side so the bucket never swings over the truck cab.
Face height must stay within the shovel's digging height; overhangs and loose boulders above the bucket are a fatal hazard.
Hydraulic oil at 300 bar injects through skin -- never search for a leak with your hand.
ar_tips: Place the shovel and the dumper together on open ground to show why the bucket must clear a 6.1 m loading height.
Walk round to the front: the bucket teeth sit about 10 m from the machine centre, which is the whole digging envelope in one view.

parts.label: Crawler tracks
parts.note: Two independently driven crawlers, 750 mm shoes. Ground bearing pressure is only about 2.2 kg/cm2 -- roughly a walking person -- which is how a 140 t machine works on a soft floor.

parts.label: Drive sprockets & idlers
parts.note: Travel motor and planetary drive at the sprocket end; track tension is set hydraulically at the idler. Shovels travel very little -- undercarriage wear comes mostly from swing and dig reaction forces.

parts.label: Car body & swing circle
parts.note: The car body ties the crawlers together and carries the swing bearing. All power and oil to the upper works passes through the centre swivel inside this ring.

parts.label: Superstructure (house)
parts.note: Carries the diesel engine (about 600-800 kW), the main hydraulic pumps, oil coolers and tanks. Everything above the swing circle rotates 360 degrees.

parts.label: Engine & cooling pack
parts.note: Diesel-hydraulic drive: the engine turns variable-displacement pumps, and oil does all the work. Electric-drive versions trail a cable and cut fuel cost where the pit layout allows it.

parts.label: Counterweight
parts.note: Balances the loaded bucket at full reach. Removing or under-specifying it is what turns a hard dig into a tipping incident.

parts.label: Operator cab (FOPS)
parts.note: Mounted high on the left front for a clear view into the bucket. Falling-Object Protective Structure plus a rock deflector; the operator sits about 5 m up.

parts.label: Cab glazing
parts.note: Large front and roof windows -- the operator must watch the bucket teeth, the face above, and the truck being loaded.

parts.label: Walkways & handrails
parts.note: Service access to pumps, filters and the cooling pack. Isolate and lock out hydraulics before any work on the upper works.

parts.label: Access ladder
parts.note: Retractable stairway, raised while digging. The machine must be shut down and the bucket grounded before anyone climbs.

parts.label: Boom
parts.note: Fabricated box-section arm pinned to the house front. On a face shovel the boom is short and steep -- it is built to resist crowd forces into a vertical face rather than to reach down.

parts.label: Stick (dipper arm)
parts.note: Carries the bucket and provides the crowd force that drives the teeth into the face. Stick length trades reach against breakout force.

parts.label: Bucket (7.5 m3)
parts.note: Bottom-dump face-shovel bucket: the floor unlatches and swings open to release the load. Four passes fill a 220 t dumper, so bucket size must match truck size -- that is the match factor.

parts.label: Teeth & GET
parts.note: Ground Engaging Tools: replaceable tooth adapters, side cutters and wear plates. Worn teeth raise dig time and fuel burn, and a tooth lost into the load can wreck a crusher.

parts.label: Hydraulic cylinders
parts.note: Boom-hoist pair, stick cylinder and bucket cylinder, working at roughly 300-350 bar. Breakout force at the teeth -- not engine power -- is the shovel's real digging rating.

parts.label: 1.8 m person (for scale)
parts.note: A person in PPE, 1.8 m tall, standing clear of the machine. Use the scale toggle to hide them. In real AR at 1:1 you can simply walk up to the machine yourself.
